text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A trilateral agreement signed by Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov and heads of Azeri and Chechen oil companies in Baku on July 11 proved that economic interests dominate political ones.
- An otherwise quiet Saturday night in Moscow was disrupted by a bomb explosion near the Main Military Prosecutor's Office, but no one was hurt.
- Russian capital previously taken abroad has started returning to the country in the form of foreign investments, some experts say.
- Distribution of the federal budget money is a major stumbling block in relations between regional governors and the president's representatives to the regions.
-- Muscovites like the outer Moscow ring road, or bypass, which has been undergoing major repairs, because it is comfortable and fast, the newspaper says.
